excerpt: Dr. Elena Rodriguez of Dana-Farber writes that the NIH’s sudden termination of grants studying single-cell resistance in triple-negative breast cancer ‘is not just a bureaucratic decision — it is a death sentence for patients who have no other options.’ She argues that cutting genomic research during an active funding freeze is akin to abandoning the front line of oncology.

Testifying before the Senate Health Committee, Dr. Whitfield of Johns Hopkins warned that the administration’s elimination of diversity-focused Alzheimer’s biomarker studies ‘will set back early detection in Black and Hispanic communities by a decade or more.’ He called the cuts ‘a form of health care discrimination through policy.’

Dr. Anika Sharma at Cleveland Clinic: ‘My deep learning MRI work on myocardial fibrosis just got defunded because it used an algorithm labeled “DEI‐adjacent.” This is not efficiency—it's ideology over patients. I’ll be joining the #StandUpForScience rally in D.C. next week.’

At a WashU town hall, Dr. Marquez said that HHS’s new restrictions on international collaborations have halted her lab’s work on carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella. ‘I have postdocs whose visas were flagged for “sensitive research” on a bacteria that kills 50,000 Americans a year. This is bureaucracy weaponized against public health.’

Dr. Latoya Jackson, speaking on North Carolina public TV, said that Trump’s freeze on community-based hypertension research in rural Black communities ‘is hurting the very people who trusted us. We can’t hold blood pressure screenings if our funding is cut for not being “patriotic enough.”’

Dr. Gomez at UTHSCSA posted: ‘ICE agents showing up at community health centers on the border? That’s the real toxin driving preterm birth—not my research. The administration is using immigration enforcement to terrorize pregnant women into silence.’

UCSF announces that Dr. Ava Thompson’s technology-based PrEP intervention for transgender women has completed enrollment. Early data show a 40% increase in uptake among participants using the mobile app compared to standard care.

Dr. Hart of Boston Children’s Hospital, alongside 50+ pediatric endocrinologists, signed an open letter decrying the new HHS rule that categorizes gender-affirming care research as ‘non-essential.’ The letter states that ‘blocking these longitudinal studies will directly harm the mental health of transgender and non-binary adolescents.’

Dr. Samuel Osei of Emory discussed his community-driven vaccine narrative project, noting that personalized stories have reduced hesitancy by 25% in focus groups. He emphasized that the work is ‘about trust, not politics.’

University of Michigan announces that Dr. Priya Sharma’s team has identified a novel epigenetic marker in podocytes that predicts progression of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, opening a potential therapeutic target.

Terminating grants that study structural racism and cardiovascular health isn't just bad policy—it's a direct attack on the lives of Black communities. My patients deserve better than this administration's willful ignorance.

By slashing funding for research on redlining and clinical trial participation, we're not just losing data—we're entrenching cancer disparities that will kill Black women for decades. This is an act of public health sabotage.
The administration's cancellation of community-based nutrition interventions directly harms pregnant people in food deserts. It will increase preterm births and widen disparities, plain and simple.
When you criminalize LGBTQ+ youth and cut substance use funding, you're not protecting anyone—you're pushing kids into worse outcomes. This is a moral failure, not a budget choice.
Our multi-cohort study shows that wildfire smoke from climate change increases preterm birth risk by 15%. These findings underscore the urgent need for climate adaptation in maternal health.
The PEARL trial is testing a more precise thrombolytic approach for intermediate-risk PE. Early data suggest we can reduce bleeding complications while maintaining efficacy.

Deporting community health workers in rural Texas is tearing apart the very network that prevents maternal deaths among Black women. This administration's immigration policy is a death sentence for my patients.
Cutting EPA monitoring and NIH funding for agricultural worker health is unconscionable—these workers face particulate exposures that damage their hearts, and we're turning our backs on them.

Our latest findings on broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the hemagglutinin stem could lead to a universal flu vaccine. Proud of the team's progress, but we need stable federal funding to continue.
